# Discover
Seed: You are a lighthouse keeper looking after a light on a quiet coast. · "a cosy game about running a lighthouse" (the creative's words) · last run 2026-11-09

BMUZ collects the bricks here; nothing in this file is chosen. Choosing which bricks to build with is /define's. Lines are only ever added or annotated, never removed: edit anything you like, your edits are kept.

### Theme — subject notes, references in/out of games, tone words, what players already know
- Seen, heard, touched: Wet stone and salt air on the cliff path, the hum of the lamp, the slow creak of the tower door. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Seen, heard, touched: Foghorn bells and gulls, the glow of a warm lamp room against a grey sea. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Seen, heard, touched: Brass and glass of the lens, cold metal rail under a glove, a kettle on the stove. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Everyone already knows: Lighthouses guide ships at night, and people already picture the beam sweeping across dark water. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Everyone already knows: The keeper's routine of logs, lamps and checks is a familiar image from stories and films. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- From the creative's life: Watching a light come on at dusk on a long walk by the coast. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Outside games: Film and books about remote keepers, a cosy-mystery feel, shipping forecasts on the radio, a ritual of tending a fire or a garden. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Tone: Cosy and quiet, with a faint melancholy and warmth from the company of the light. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Offshore keeper rota: about two weeks on the light, one week ashore, with supplies every two weeks weather permitting — run 1 · [Keeper's Life (Chesapeake Chapter, US Lighthouse Society, Cheslights Kids)](https://www.cheslights.org/cheskids/html/keepers-life.htm) · one source
- Fog bell rung in patterns by hand before the lamp was automated (a sound-signal tradition) — run 1 · [Keeper's Life (Chesapeake Chapter, US Lighthouse Society, Cheslights Kids)](https://www.cheslights.org/cheskids/html/keepers-life.htm) · one source
- Handwritten daily logbook: short dated entries of work, weather, ships and inspections, one a day — run 1 · [Lighthouse Keepers' Log (NPS, Point Reyes 1888 log)](https://www.nps.gov/pore/learn/historyculture/stories_maritime_keeperslog.htm) · one source
- Keeper's Sunday and holiday rest: 'Thanksgiving - No work' in the 1888 log — run 1 · [Lighthouse Keepers' Log (NPS, Point Reyes 1888 log)](https://www.nps.gov/pore/learn/historyculture/stories_maritime_keeperslog.htm) · one source
- Double Fine's Keeper: the lighthouse walks as a character and its light revives a dying land — run 1 · [Keeper (PC) Review - CGMagazine](https://www.cgmagonline.com/review/game/keeper-pc/) · one source
- Keepers had no days off; the night job was repetitive, and it was the lonely, unshowy kind of work · tone: lonely, dutiful, warm — run 1 · [A Day in the Life of a Lighthouse Keeper (Save the Light)](https://savethelight.org/blog/a-day-in-the-life-of-a-lighthouse-keeper/), [Static Dread: The Lighthouse Turns Papers, Please Into Eldritch Horror Review (Sidequesting)](https://www.sidequesting.com/2025/09/static-dread-the-lighthouse-turns-papers-please-into-eldritch-horror-review) · several sources
- The keeper's craft was passed on by lampists and keepers who were lost when the lights were automated · tone: wistful, a loss to mourn — run 1 · [Point Reyes Lighthouse Lens Receives Special Care (NPS)](https://www.nps.gov/pore/learn/news/newsreleases_20041214_lhlens.htm), [Boston Light has stood since 1716 and was automated in 1998, but Congress kept a keeper on it (inkl)](https://www.inkl.com/news/boston-light-has-stood-since-1716-and-was-automated-in-1998-but-congress-kept-a-keeper-on-it-when-sally-snowman-retired-in-2023-the-us-lost-its-last-one) · several sources
- Isolation is the normal condition: a wife at a remote station felt she gave up nearly all social life · tone: quiet, faintly melancholy — run 1 · ["When a woman marries a lighthouse keeper..." (NPS)](https://www.nps.gov/apis/learn/historyculture/ihatelighthouses.htm) · one source
- North Foreland, the last manned UK lighthouse, was automated on 26 Nov 1998, ending about four centuries of keeping · folklore tone — run 1 · [A fine farewell - Trinity House](https://www.trinityhouse.co.uk/articles/a-fine-farewell) · one source
- Stag lights: stations run only by men, with no family on site · isolated, rugged — run 1 · [Lighthouse keeper - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lighthouse_keeper) · one source
- Bishop Rock 1946: a BBC commentator stranded 29 days, 'I wore the same shirt' · hardship with dry humour — run 1 · [A fine farewell - Trinity House](https://www.trinityhouse.co.uk/articles/a-fine-farewell) · one source
- Retired keepers still live in lighthouse cottages and look after their stations · continuity, warmth — run 1 · [A fine farewell - Trinity House](https://www.trinityhouse.co.uk/articles/a-fine-farewell) · one source
- Automation came in stages from the 1960s, with keepers replaced over the late 20th century · a lost human presence — run 1 · [Lighthouse keeper - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lighthouse_keeper) · one source
- Lighthouse keeping as a ritual of fixed chores: fuel, wick, polish, wind, watch, log, in a shift rota — run 1 · [The Keepers (NPS Cape Hatteras National Seashore, FAQs)](https://www.nps.gov/caha/learn/historyculture/thekeepersfaqs.htm), [Lighthouse keeper duties (National Records of Scotland)](https://nrscotland.gov.uk/learning-and-events/for-the-safety-of-all-scotlands-lighthouses/lighthouse-keeper-duties/) · several sources
- Automation took the people off the rock and moved the tending to a remote office in Edinburgh (208 lights, one control room) — run 1 · [The Automation of Lighthouses (Ways of Life, Substack)](https://waysoflife.substack.com/p/the-automation-of-lighthouses) · one source
- Keepers' wives' sewing circles, parties and birthday cakes: company made by small rituals on an isolated island — run 1 · [Apostle Islands Scrapbook (McLean)](https://www.bobmackreth.com/Scrapbook/mcclean.htm) · one source
- Arbroath flag and clothing signals to tell a keeper on the rock that a baby had been born — run 1 · [Lighthouse keeper duties (National Records of Scotland)](https://nrscotland.gov.uk/learning-and-events/for-the-safety-of-all-scotlands-lighthouses/lighthouse-keeper-duties/) · one source
- Each light had its own flash signature so sailors could tell it from its neighbours (fixed, flashing, group-flashing) — run 1 · [Light characteristic (Wikipedia), search result only](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light_characteristic) · one source
- Lighthouse keeping was cost-driven: keepers went when maintenance was judged too expensive, and staffing lasted longest for sovereignty reasons (Machias Seal Island) — run 1 · [Phares (The Canadian Encyclopedia), search result only](https://thecanadianencyclopedia.ca/en/article/phares) · one source
- Tower upkeep paid by 'light dues' on shipping tonnage — run 1 · [The Automation of Lighthouses (Ways of Life, Substack)](https://waysoflife.substack.com/p/the-automation-of-lighthouses) · one source

### Nouns — thing · attributes/states · acts or acted on · motivation/conflict (living things)
- lamp (and wick) · states: unlit / lit / burning / guttering / needs wick trimmed / smoking / sooted / fuel low / out · acts / acted on: acted on by oil, wick and soot, and by dusk and dawn; the keeper fuels, trims and lights it; a smoking wick dims the lens — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- lens (Fresnel) · states: clean / smudged / dull / polished / sun-discoloured / curtained by day / turning / stopped · acts / acted on: acted on by the keeper's cloth, salt and smoke (smudge), sunlight (discolour), curtains (shield), clockwork (turns it) — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- clockwork weight · states: wound / running / running down / stopped / needs lubricating · acts / acted on: turns the lens and drives the bells; the keeper winds it by hand; a missed winding stops it — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- fog bell or fog signal · states: silent / ringing in pattern / ringing / out of order · acts / acted on: acted on by the keeper's hand and by fog, which sets when it must run — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- logbook · states: blank / written / signed off / inspected / missed · acts / acted on: acted on by the keeper's pen, the day's weather and ships; the next keeper reads it — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- keeper (living) · states: on watch / resting / ashore / sick / handing over / rotating out · acts / acted on: acts on lamp, lens, bell, log; acted on by storm and supply boat · wants: to keep the light burning through the night, company, news, supplies, a rest ashore, a relief on rota · stopped by: storm, long weather delays, isolation, homesickness, relief delays, supply cut off — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- ship (living crew) · states: approaching / passing / in fog / lost · acts / acted on: reads the light's flash pattern to find itself · wants: to know which light it sees and where the rocks are · stopped by: a light it cannot tell from its neighbours, fog, haze, rocks and reefs — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- fog · states: clear / hazy / dense · acts / acted on: hides the light; acted on by the fog signal and radio beacon as backups — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- lamp (and its wick) · states: unlit / lit / burning / guttering / needs wick trimmed / smoking / sooted / fuel-low / out · acts on / acted on by: oil, wick, soot, dusk and dawn; the keeper fuels, trims and lights it; a smoking wick dims the lens — run 1 · [Keeper's Life (Chesapeake Chapter, US Lighthouse Society, Cheslights Kids)](https://www.cheslights.org/cheskids/html/keepers-life.htm), [The Keepers (NPS Cape Hatteras National Seashore, FAQs)](https://www.nps.gov/caha/learn/historyculture/thekeepersfaqs.htm), [A Day in the Life of a Lighthouse Keeper (Save the Light)](https://savethelight.org/blog/a-day-in-the-life-of-a-lighthouse-keeper/), [Point Reyes Lighthouse Lens Receives Special Care (NPS)](https://www.nps.gov/pore/learn/news/newsreleases_20041214_lhlens.htm) · several sources
- lens (Fresnel) · states: clean / smudged / dull / polished / sun-discoloured / curtained by day / covered at night / turning / stopped · acts on / acted on by: the beam; the keeper's cloth and polishing; salt and smoke smudge it, which reduces the light; sunlight discolours it; curtains shield it; the clockwork turns it — run 1 · [A Day in the Life of a Lighthouse Keeper (Save the Light)](https://savethelight.org/blog/a-day-in-the-life-of-a-lighthouse-keeper/), [Keeper's Life (Chesapeake Chapter, US Lighthouse Society, Cheslights Kids)](https://www.cheslights.org/cheskids/html/keepers-life.htm), [The Keepers (NPS Cape Hatteras National Seashore, FAQs)](https://www.nps.gov/caha/learn/historyculture/thekeepersfaqs.htm) · several sources

### Verbs — theme word → outcome form · combines with → skill
- trim → keep the flame steady and smoke-free so the beam stays bright · combines with: lamp-care skill with polish and wind — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- polish → clean the lens and brass so the beam carries farther · combines with: lamp-care skill — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- wind → store a slow pull in the weight so the lens keeps turning through the night · combines with: lamp-care skill — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- ring → send a timed pattern on the fog bell so ships hear the coast · combines with: signalling skill with flash — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- flash → repeat a timed pattern of colour and light so a ship can tell which light it sees · combines with: signalling skill with ring — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- log → write the day into a dated record the next keeper can trust · combines with: record skill — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- relight → restore the light by hand after a storm, with limited tools · combines with: lamp-care skill — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- shutter → cover the lens by day so the sun cannot discolour it · combines with: lamp-care skill — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- haul → carry water, fuel and supplies up the tower so the house and lamp keep going · combines with: upkeep skill — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- rotate watch → share the night between keepers in turns · combines with: upkeep skill — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- bloom → shine the light on a plant so it revives (from Keeper, Double Fine: prior art, not chosen) · combines with: not combined; outside the lighthouse loop — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Skill: lamp care = trim / polish / wind / relight / shutter — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Skill: signalling = ring / flash — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Skill: record keeping = log — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Skill: upkeep and supply = haul / rotate watch — run 1 · Claude's suggestion

### Verb × noun grid — what each verb does to each noun; empty/surprising cells flagged
- trim × lamp: steadies the flame, stops smoke — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- trim × lens: nothing (empty) — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- polish × lens: clears smudge so the beam carries farther — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- polish × clockwork weight: nothing (empty) — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- wind × clockwork weight: keeps the lens turning — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- wind × fog bell: bell keeps its pattern when the weight is wound (surprising) — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- ring × fog bell: sounds the pattern a ship can hear through fog — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- flash × lamp: a timed flash lets a ship name which light it sees — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- log × keeper: a record the next keeper reads, which can also show when a keeper is due to rest (surprising) — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- shutter × lens: shields the glass from sun — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- haul × lamp: brings fuel and oil that keep it burning — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- haul × keeper: carries supplies up to the keeper — run 1 · Claude's suggestion

### Decisions — candidate choices and their tradeoffs
- Choice: wind the clockwork now, or leave it to run down until the next cycle — costs: lens stops turning and the beam dims at a sailor's key moment — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Choice: polish the lens in the day, or rest for the next watch — costs: less shine by night, more rest — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Choice: ring the fog bell when the fog thickens, or keep it quiet — costs: ships hear the coast, but the keeper's stamina and oil run down — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Problem the player solves: Keep the lamp burning through the night so ships can find the coast. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Problem the player solves: Keep ships from confusing this light with its neighbours. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Problem the player solves: Keep the keeper fed, rested and supplied through long weather and isolation. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- a neighbour's request with a short expiry → costs: stress, which the no-failure, cosy constraint rules out — run 1 · [Why Cozy Games Are Harder to Make Than They Look (Urgame Tips)](https://urgametips.com/why-cozy-games-are-harder-to-make-than-they-look/) · one source
- upgrades or rewards that arrive too fast or too slow → costs: too fast gives no reason to stay; too slow makes the game feel static — run 1 · [Why Cozy Games Are Harder to Make Than They Look (Urgame Tips)](https://urgametips.com/why-cozy-games-are-harder-to-make-than-they-look/) · one source
- keep the loop short and end before it repeats → costs: less to do per session, so the chore risk is lower but the depth is shallower (Static Dread's ending was praised for stopping before it got repetitive) — run 1 · [Static Dread: The Lighthouse Turns Papers, Please Into Eldritch Horror Review (Sidequesting)](https://www.sidequesting.com/2025/09/static-dread-the-lighthouse-turns-papers-please-into-eldritch-horror-review) · one source
- clean the lens on a schedule vs when it looks dull → costs: field data show the cleaning interval changed the loss very little, so effort may buy little shine (solar panels, not lenses) — run 1 · [Photovoltaic performance degradation due to soiling and characteristics (HBKU ELMI)](https://elmi.hbku.edu.qa/en/publications/photovoltaic-performance-degradation-due-to-soiling-and-character/) · one source

### Mechanism shelf — outcome verb → candidate mechanisms → example games → skill it teaches
- Feels like the verb: clean the lens and brass → aim and hold a beam on a target until it changes (Keeper's aim-and-hold; the target there is a plant, so it's a close match, not proven for a lens) — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Feels like the verb: store a slow pull in the weight → a stored reserve that runs down on its own clock and is wound back up by hand, with two knobs: how much is stored and how fast it is spent — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Feels like the verb: ring the fog bell → a timed pattern on a fixed interval, like real lights and fog signals, so ships can tell the coast by its rhythm — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Feels like the verb: trim the lamp → a steady level kept by a drain and a refill (a resource pattern from Björk & Holopainen; the flame case is unsourced) — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Feels pasted on: flame steadiness as a producer/consumer flow: a resource pattern without a game that does it, so it could feel like a spreadsheet — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Feels pasted on: restart-style upkeep (turn the generator back on, restart the rotation): critics called this dull and repetitive, and it doesn't fit the cosy brief — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Feels pasted on: fetch-and-travel hauling: the Locomoto reviewer found waiting on each trip boring — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Feels pasted on: sending a companion to points (Keeper's Twig): a verb that belongs to another game, not to the lighthouse's own work — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Genre that already covers some verbs: Adventure puzzle games already bundle light-aiming with companion-sending (Keeper is the sourced example), so the aim and signal parts have precedent. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Genre that already covers some verbs: Cozy games already build on mundane tasks; the risk is that they become a checklist unless each task has a clear purpose and payoff. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Genre that already covers some verbs: No lighthouse keeper-sim or tending genre bundle was sourced, so the bundle of keeping a light, polishing and timed signalling is the part we'd have to invent or check with the creative. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- keep the flame steady and smoke-free → keep a resource level steady with a producer / consumer flow → example games: none sourced in this run → teaches: budgeting a drain against a refill — run 1 · [Table of contents for Patterns in game design (Björk & Holopainen)](https://catdir.loc.gov/catdir/toc/ecip052/2004023500.html) · one source
- clean the lens and brass → aim and hold a beam on the target until it changes → example games: Keeper (its target there is a plant, not a lens) → teaches: hold aim steady on a target until it changes — run 1 · [Keeper gameplay preview (Xbox Wire)](https://news.xbox.com/en-us/2025/08/20/keeper-gameplay-preview/), [Keeper review: the best trip of the year (Galaxus)](https://www.galaxus.ch/en/page/keeper-review-the-best-trip-of-the-year-40023) · several sources

### Twists — constraints, SCAMPER moves, strip-downs, mashups, extremes
- Take away: the day chores, so the night at the lamp is the whole game. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Take away: the player never sees the sea and learns only from the logbook and ships' reactions. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Take away: a ship never says whether it read the signal; the only feedback is its heading changing. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Mashup: Keeper's walking lighthouse plus Static Dread's day-and-night routine, with the lighthouse making the trip to ships. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Mashup: the Tamagotchi sleep rule applied to the lens, so the light rests under its shutter by day and is tended only at dusk and dawn. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Constraint: a meter that drains but never ends the run, only dims the light, so a missed chore has a visible cost with no game over (The Wickie's idea). — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Extreme: One real-time night watch per session, with the day skipped, so the whole game is one watch. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Extreme: A signal with a cost: the beam can be used too hard and has to rest, the lesson from Cagibi's spammed beam. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Twist, take away: remove the day chores and make the night at the lamp the whole game, one short night per play. — run 1 · [Static Dread: The Lighthouse Turns Papers, Please Into Eldritch Horror Review (SideQuesting)](https://www.sidequesting.com/2025/09/static-dread-the-lighthouse-turns-papers-please-into-eldritch-horror-review) · one source
- Twist, take away: the player never sees the lamp or the sea and learns only from the logbook and ships' reactions. — run 1 · [The Keepers (Cape Hatteras National Seashore, NPS FAQ)](https://home.nps.gov/caha/learn/historyculture/thekeepersfaqs.htm) · one source
- Twist, take away: the ship never says whether it read the signal; the only feedback is its heading changing. — run 1 · [Double Fine's latest gem fails to attract players on Steam (Gamereactor)](https://www.gamereactor.eu/double-fines-latest-gem-fails-to-attract-players-on-steam-1619923/) · one source
- Mashup: Keeper's walking lighthouse plus Static Dread's day/night routine, with the lighthouse taking the trip to meet ships. — run 1 · [Keeper on Steam (Double Fine / Lee Petty, 2025)](https://store.steampowered.com/app/3043580/Keeper/), [Static Dread: The Lighthouse review: Something wicked this way comes (Shacknews)](https://www.shacknews.com/article/145404/static-dread-the-lighthouse-review-something-wicked-this-way-comes) · several sources
- Mashup: the Tamagotchi sleep rule applied to the lens, so the light is asleep under its shutter by day and tending happens only at dusk and dawn. — run 1 · [Mental Floss, Tamagotchi history](https://mentalfloss.com/article/642373/tamagotchi-history) · one source
- Extreme: a single real-time night watch per session, with the day skipped, so the whole game is one watch. — run 1 · [The Keepers (Cape Hatteras National Seashore, NPS FAQ)](https://home.nps.gov/caha/learn/historyculture/thekeepersfaqs.htm) · one source

### Hopes & fears — fears carried as assumptions with evidence status
- Hope: It feels cosy and unhurried, with small daily jobs that feel good to finish. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Hope: A slow sense of place builds as the coast and its visitors become familiar. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Fear: It becomes a chore with nothing to look forward to. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Fear: Too little to do, so the cosy feel turns into boredom. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Fear: Hard to keep the light and the sea reading clearly on a phone screen. — run 1 · Claude's suggestion
- Fear "It becomes a chore with nothing to look forward to.": no evidence by the Theme dig research — run 1 · Theme dig research
- Fear "Too little to do, so the cosy feel turns into boredom.": supported by the Theme dig research — Game reviews support the fear: Destructoid found Keeper limited to a few buttons and wanted more work, and CGM called its gameplay 'fairly straightforward'. One remote station (Stannard Rock) had long idle stretches with cribbage as the only named pastime. The full historical duty lists contradict it for a working keeper. The supported reading is about games and one remote station, not the historical day. ([Keeper review (Destructoid)](https://www.destructoid.com/keeper-review/), [Keeper (PC) Review - CGMagazine](https://www.cgmagonline.com/review/game/keeper-pc/), [Stannard Rock Light: The Loneliest Place in The World - Amusing Planet](https://www.amusingplanet.com/2020/01/stannard-rock-light-loneliest-place-in.html), [The Keepers (NPS Cape Hatteras National Seashore, FAQs)](https://www.nps.gov/caha/learn/historyculture/thekeepersfaqs.htm)) — run 1 · Theme dig research
- Fear "Hard to keep the light and the sea reading clearly on a phone screen.": no evidence by the Theme dig research — run 1 · Theme dig research
- Fear "It becomes a chore with nothing to look forward to.": supported by the Mechanisms research — Critics and players describe routine upkeep as dull and wearing thin (Keeper headline 'Keeper Can Feel Like a Chore to Play'; Static Dread review 'boring repetition'; a lighthouse-keeper forum review says the loop wears thin later). Solar-panel soiling data suggest cleaning how often may pay off little (a reading, not lens data). No player study was found; Urgame Tips offers rewards as the fix, which is advice, not evidence against the fear. ([Keeper Review: A Beautiful But Flawed Adventure (Gamer Rant)](https://gamerant.com/keeper-review/), [Static Dread: The Lighthouse Turns Papers, Please Into Eldritch Horror Review (Sidequesting)](https://www.sidequesting.com/2025/09/static-dread-the-lighthouse-turns-papers-please-into-eldritch-horror-review), [Review | No One Lives Under the Lighthouse (Playday forum)](https://forum.playday.one/t/review-no-one-lives-under-the-lighthouse/16270), [Photovoltaic performance degradation due to soiling and characteristics (HBKU ELMI)](https://elmi.hbku.edu.qa/en/publications/photovoltaic-performance-degradation-due-to-soiling-and-character/), [Why Cozy Games Are Harder to Make Than They Look (Urgame Tips)](https://urgametips.com/why-cozy-games-are-harder-to-make-than-they-look/)) — run 1 · Mechanisms research
- Fear "Too little to do, so the cosy feel turns into boredom.": supported by the Mechanisms research — Reviewers say Keeper's additions are 'not substantial enough to challenge the player' and its puzzles are thin and short; dbltap calls its puzzles 'not especially difficult'; Locomoto's reviewer was 'already done' before the second area. Counter-evidence: a Neowin summary says players are emotionally invested despite little gameplay, and Urgame Tips says downtime works if intentional. Mixed, and secondhand. ([Keeper Review: A Beautiful But Flawed Adventure (Gamer Rant)](https://gamerant.com/keeper-review/), [Keeper review: Light on answers and heavy on wonder (Neowin)](https://www.neowin.net/reviews/keeper-review-light-on-answers-and-heavy-on-wonder-a-must-play-double-fine-adventure/), [Keeper review: Weird and wonderful with a few imperfections (DBLTap)](https://www.dbltap.com/reviews/keeper-review), [Locomoto Review: Coziness at Its Most Boring (Gaming Trend)](https://gamingtrend.com/reviews/locomoto-review-coziness-at-its-most-boring/), [Keeper review: Light on answers and heavy on wonder, a must-play Double Fine adventure (Neowin); HTTP 403, search summary only](https://www.neowin.net/amp/keeper-review-light-on-answers-and-heavy-on-wonder-a-must-play-double-fine-adventure/), [Why Cozy Games Are Harder to Make Than They Look (Urgame Tips)](https://urgametips.com/why-cozy-games-are-harder-to-make-than-they-look/)) — run 1 · Mechanisms research
- Fear "Hard to keep the light and the sea reading clearly on a phone screen.": no evidence by the Mechanisms research — run 1 · Mechanisms research
- Fear "It becomes a chore with nothing to look forward to.": supported by the Prior art research — Chores are named as the complaint in The Lightkeeper review ('mostly mundane chores'), and a snippet calls Static Dread's upkeep repetitive (unverified). Keeper Lit is a daily checklist with no player reaction on record. Against it: Static Dread's Shacknews reviewer says it 'never overstayed its welcome', and Lighthouse Keeper (Stratera) is 80% positive despite thin duties. No source tests a no-fail daily loop, so the fear is named by sources, not measured. ([The Lightkeeper review (Adventure Game Hotspot)](https://adventuregamehotspot.com/review/6193/the-lightkeeper), [Steam Community :: Lighthouse Keeper reviews (search snippet only, not opened)](https://steamcommunity.com/app/2023050/reviews/?browsefilter=toprated), [Keeper Lit (Lapwing Studio, itch.io)](https://lapwing-studio.itch.io/keeper-lit), [Static Dread: The Lighthouse review: Something wicked this way comes (Shacknews)](https://www.shacknews.com/article/145404/static-dread-the-lighthouse-review-something-wicked-this-way-comes), [Lighthouse Keeper on Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/2023050)) — run 1 · Prior art research
- Fear "Too little to do, so the cosy feel turns into boredom.": supported by the Prior art research — Keeper is called 'too simple' and 'not exactly a complex game', with 'very little instruction on what your next move should be'; The Lightkeeper has a slow first half; Cagibi says the beginning can be 'easy/boring'; a TechRadar headline says 'lacking a little in depth'. Against it: the Keeper reviewer named low challenge but is a fan of puzzle solving, and the Gamereactor low player count gives no cause, so it does not show boredom. ([Keeper Review: A Wonderfully Weird Experience (GamingBible)](https://www.gamingbible.com/reviews/keeper-review-wonderfully-weird-experience-934692-20251017), [Keeper Review – Light and Magic (Player2)](https://www.player2.net.au/2025/10/keeper-review-light-and-magic/), [The Lightkeeper review (Adventure Game Hotspot)](https://adventuregamehotspot.com/review/6193/the-lightkeeper), [Lighthouse Keeper Postmortem: things learned & late bugs (cagibi, itch.io devlog)](https://cagibi.itch.io/lighthouse-keeper/devlog/139552/lighthouse-keeper-postmortem-things-learned-late-bugs), [Keeper review (TechRadar), headline only](https://www.techradar.com/gaming/keeper-review), [Double Fine's latest gem fails to attract players on Steam (Gamereactor)](https://www.gamereactor.eu/double-fines-latest-gem-fails-to-attract-players-on-steam-1619923/)) — run 1 · Prior art research
- Fear "Hard to keep the light and the sea reading clearly on a phone screen.": no evidence by the Prior art research — run 1 · Prior art research

## Runs (newest first)

### Run 1 — 2026-11-09 — a cosy game about running a lighthouse
<!-- bmuz run key: 1794254759498 -->
- Brief, in the creative's words: "a cosy game about running a lighthouse"
- You are: You are a lighthouse keeper looking after a light on a quiet coast.
- Steps run: spark, experience, theme, theme-dig, simulation, mechanisms, mechanism-shelf, prior-art, twists
- Research questions:
  1. What does a lighthouse keeper's day actually involve, hour by hour?
  2. How have lighthouses been kept and automated over history, and what was lost?
  3. What do the lamp, lens and tower need to keep working, and what wears out?
  4. What do the people who sail past a coast want and fear from a light?
  5. How do keepers and their families live in isolated places, and what do they do for comfort?
- Bricks added: [Spark](#spark) 7 · [Hopes & fears](#hopes-fears) 14 · [On ice](#on-ice) 55 · [Experience goals](#experience-goals) 30 · [Theme](#theme) 28 · [Nouns](#nouns) 16 · [Verbs](#verbs) 26 · [Verb × noun grid](#verb-noun-grid) 12 · [Decisions](#decisions) 10 · [Prior art](#prior-art) 16 · [Mechanism shelf](#mechanism-shelf) 20 · [Hooks & anchors](#hooks-anchors) 22 · [Twists](#twists) 16 · [Open questions](#open-questions) 35
- Theme dig research: [the full report](research/discover-cosy-lighthouse-keeper-theme.md) · 41 findings, 16 backed by several sources
  - The day has clear anchors: the lamp is lit at dusk and put out at dawn, with logs, upkeep and watch in between. ([A Day in the Life of a Lighthouse Keeper (Save the Light)](https://savethelight.org/blog/a-day-in-the-life-of-a-lighthouse-keeper/), [The Keepers (NPS Cape Hatteras National Seashore, FAQs)](https://www.nps.gov/caha/learn/historyculture/thekeepersfaqs.htm)) (several sources)
  - The duty list is mostly fixed chores: fuel, wick trimming, lens and brass polishing, clockwork winding, logbook, painting, repairs, and rationing oil and water. ([The Keepers (NPS Cape Hatteras National Seashore, FAQs)](https://www.nps.gov/caha/learn/historyculture/thekeepersfaqs.htm), [Lighthouse keeper duties (National Records of Scotland)](https://nrscotland.gov.uk/learning-and-events/for-the-safety-of-all-scotlands-lighthouses/lighthouse-keeper-duties/), [Lighthouse Keepers' Log (NPS, Point Reyes 1888 log)](https://www.nps.gov/pore/learn/historyculture/stories_maritime_keeperslog.htm), [A Day in the Life of a Lighthouse Keeper (Save the Light)](https://savethelight.org/blog/a-day-in-the-life-of-a-lighthouse-keeper/), [Keeper's Life (Chesapeake Chapter, US Lighthouse Society, Cheslights Kids)](https://www.cheslights.org/cheskids/html/keepers-life.htm)) (several sources)
  - Night watches ran in three or four hour turns that rotated daily, and the keeper on the last watch did the morning lamp and lens upkeep. ([The Keepers (NPS Cape Hatteras National Seashore, FAQs)](https://www.nps.gov/caha/learn/historyculture/thekeepersfaqs.htm), [Lighthouse keeper duties (National Records of Scotland)](https://nrscotland.gov.uk/learning-and-events/for-the-safety-of-all-scotlands-lighthouses/lighthouse-keeper-duties/)) (several sources)
  - Keeping the daily record was part of the routine: a dated logbook of work, weather, ships and inspections. ([Lighthouse Keepers' Log (NPS, Point Reyes 1888 log)](https://www.nps.gov/pore/learn/historyculture/stories_maritime_keeperslog.htm), [Keeper's Life (Chesapeake Chapter, US Lighthouse Society, Cheslights Kids)](https://www.cheslights.org/cheskids/html/keepers-life.htm), [A Day in the Life of a Lighthouse Keeper (Save the Light)](https://savethelight.org/blog/a-day-in-the-life-of-a-lighthouse-keeper/), [The Keepers (NPS Cape Hatteras National Seashore, FAQs)](https://www.nps.gov/caha/learn/historyculture/thekeepersfaqs.htm)) (several sources)
  - Lights were automated in stages: the US from early in the 20th century with a major push in the early 1960s, the UK from the 1960s, and the last manned UK lighthouse (North Foreland) in 1998. ([Boston Light has stood since 1716 and was automated in 1998, but Congress kept a keeper on it (inkl)](https://www.inkl.com/news/boston-light-has-stood-since-1716-and-was-automated-in-1998-but-congress-kept-a-keeper-on-it-when-sally-snowman-retired-in-2023-the-us-lost-its-last-one), [A fine farewell - Trinity House](https://www.trinityhouse.co.uk/articles/a-fine-farewell), [Lighthouse keeper - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lighthouse_keeper)) (several sources)
  - The move to automate was mainly financial, and in Canada cost decided which lights kept keepers, with Machias Seal Island staying staffed for sovereignty reasons. ([The Automation of Lighthouses (Ways of Life, Substack)](https://waysoflife.substack.com/p/the-automation-of-lighthouses), [Phares (The Canadian Encyclopedia), search result only](https://thecanadianencyclopedia.ca/en/article/phares)) (several sources)
  - Remaining keepers do upkeep, buoy repair and maintenance of automated systems, and some retired keepers still live in lighthouse cottages and look after their stations. ([Lighthouse keeper - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lighthouse_keeper), [A fine farewell - Trinity House](https://www.trinityhouse.co.uk/articles/a-fine-farewell)) (several sources)
  - The lens needs daily cleaning, and a smudge on it reduces its effectiveness; salt and smoke also smudge it. ([A Day in the Life of a Lighthouse Keeper (Save the Light)](https://savethelight.org/blog/a-day-in-the-life-of-a-lighthouse-keeper/), [The Keepers (NPS Cape Hatteras National Seashore, FAQs)](https://www.nps.gov/caha/learn/historyculture/thekeepersfaqs.htm)) (several sources)
  - The lamp wick needs trimming and soot cleaning so the flame burns steady and bright without smoking. ([Keeper's Life (Chesapeake Chapter, US Lighthouse Society, Cheslights Kids)](https://www.cheslights.org/cheskids/html/keepers-life.htm), [A Day in the Life of a Lighthouse Keeper (Save the Light)](https://savethelight.org/blog/a-day-in-the-life-of-a-lighthouse-keeper/), [Point Reyes Lighthouse Lens Receives Special Care (NPS)](https://www.nps.gov/pore/learn/news/newsreleases_20041214_lhlens.htm), [The Keepers (NPS Cape Hatteras National Seashore, FAQs)](https://www.nps.gov/caha/learn/historyculture/thekeepersfaqs.htm)) (several sources)
  - Automation swapped the clockwork and oil for machines: one Scottish source says the weight no longer exists, St Augustine turns its lens with an electric motor, and a modern lamp uses about 150 W of LEDs that are 'pretty much maintenance-free'. ([The Automation of Lighthouses (Ways of Life, Substack)](https://waysoflife.substack.com/p/the-automation-of-lighthouses), [Point Reyes Lighthouse Lens Receives Special Care (NPS)](https://www.nps.gov/pore/learn/news/newsreleases_20041214_lhlens.htm)) (several sources)
  - Fog signals and radio beacons were backups when the light could not be seen or heard, and keepers kept 'the light and fog signal in working order'. ([Lighthouse - Intensity, visibility and character of lights - Britannica](https://britannica.com/technology/lighthouse/Intensity-visibility-and-character-of-lights), [Lighthouse keeper duties (National Records of Scotland)](https://nrscotland.gov.uk/learning-and-events/for-the-safety-of-all-scotlands-lighthouses/lighthouse-keeper-duties/)) (several sources)
  - Keepers helped ships with navigation and sometimes performed rescues. ([A Day in the Life of a Lighthouse Keeper (Save the Light)](https://savethelight.org/blog/a-day-in-the-life-of-a-lighthouse-keeper/), [Lighthouse keeper - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lighthouse_keeper)) (several sources)
  - Weather could cut off supply and boat access, and in 1904 a relief delay left the Stannard Rock keepers with no food. ([Stannard Rock Light: The Loneliest Place in The World - Amusing Planet](https://www.amusingplanet.com/2020/01/stannard-rock-light-loneliest-place-in.html), [Lighthouse keeper duties (National Records of Scotland)](https://nrscotland.gov.uk/learning-and-events/for-the-safety-of-all-scotlands-lighthouses/lighthouse-keeper-duties/), [Keeper's Life (Chesapeake Chapter, US Lighthouse Society, Cheslights Kids)](https://www.cheslights.org/cheskids/html/keepers-life.htm)) (several sources)
  - Families sometimes lived on site or in nearby cottages; Stannard Rock had no wives or families, and some US 'stag lights' were run by men alone. ([Lighthouse keeper duties (National Records of Scotland)](https://nrscotland.gov.uk/learning-and-events/for-the-safety-of-all-scotlands-lighthouses/lighthouse-keeper-duties/), [Lighthouse keeper - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lighthouse_keeper), [Stannard Rock Light: The Loneliest Place in The World - Amusing Planet](https://www.amusingplanet.com/2020/01/stannard-rock-light-loneliest-place-in.html)) (several sources)
  - Station households had small domestic pleasures and chores: a cow from a neighbour, a kitchen range, a cellar milk room, a medicine chest by steamer, and hauling water and fuel. ([Lighthouse Keepers' Log (NPS, Point Reyes 1888 log)](https://www.nps.gov/pore/learn/historyculture/stories_maritime_keeperslog.htm), [Apostle Islands Scrapbook (McLean)](https://www.bobmackreth.com/Scrapbook/mcclean.htm)) (several sources)
  - Passing ships brought keepers supplies or news, and visitors and inspectors were greeted and sometimes lodged. ([A Day in the Life of a Lighthouse Keeper (Save the Light)](https://savethelight.org/blog/a-day-in-the-life-of-a-lighthouse-keeper/), [The Keepers (NPS Cape Hatteras National Seashore, FAQs)](https://www.nps.gov/caha/learn/historyculture/thekeepersfaqs.htm)) (several sources)
  Contradictions kept:
  - Work often paused on Sundays and holidays; 'Thanksgiving - No work' appears in the log. ([Lighthouse Keepers' Log (NPS, Point Reyes 1888 log)](https://www.nps.gov/pore/learn/historyculture/stories_maritime_keeperslog.htm)) (context: NPS 1888 station log (Point Reyes-era station record).) — but 'There were no days off.' ([A Day in the Life of a Lighthouse Keeper (Save the Light)](https://savethelight.org/blog/a-day-in-the-life-of-a-lighthouse-keeper/)) (context: Savethelight general blog on a keeper's day.)
  - The reviewer found the lighthouse loop satisfying, and said the game ends before the repetition goes stale. ([Static Dread: The Lighthouse Turns Papers, Please Into Eldritch Horror Review (Sidequesting)](https://www.sidequesting.com/2025/09/static-dread-the-lighthouse-turns-papers-please-into-eldritch-horror-review)) (context: Sidequesting review of Static Dread: The Lighthouse (horror game).) — but The same review calls the job 'the boring repetition of your average night job', says tracking the rules was 'needlessly frustrating', and says that with no mid-night save daytime tasks felt like a chore. ([Static Dread: The Lighthouse Turns Papers, Please Into Eldritch Horror Review (Sidequesting)](https://www.sidequesting.com/2025/09/static-dread-the-lighthouse-turns-papers-please-into-eldritch-horror-review)) (context: Same Sidequesting review, same game.)
  - Reviewers say the lighthouse duties feel pointless, and the game ends abruptly. ([Steam Community :: Lighthouse Keeper reviews (search snippet only)](https://steamcommunity.com/app/2023050/reviews/?browsefilter=toprated)) (context: 2022 Steam indie Lighthouse Keeper, built on crafting and potion-making (search snippet, not opened).) — but The loop was satisfying even though the job was built on repetition. ([Static Dread: The Lighthouse Turns Papers, Please Into Eldritch Horror Review (Sidequesting)](https://www.sidequesting.com/2025/09/static-dread-the-lighthouse-turns-papers-please-into-eldritch-horror-review)) (context: Sidequesting review of a different lighthouse-keeper game (Static Dread).)
  - Keeper's gameplay is 'fairly straightforward' but inventive, and the game earned 9/10. ([Keeper (PC) Review - CGMagazine](https://www.cgmagonline.com/review/game/keeper-pc/)) (context: CGM review of Double Fine's Keeper.) — but Gameplay is limited to a few buttons; the reviewer wanted more challenge or work done on their behalf. ([Keeper review (Destructoid)](https://www.destructoid.com/keeper-review/)) (context: Destructoid review of the same game, Keeper.)
  - The duties are long and daily (fuel, wick, lens, brass, clockwork, logbook, supplies, watches), with no quiet idle periods listed. ([The Keepers (NPS Cape Hatteras National Seashore, FAQs)](https://www.nps.gov/caha/learn/historyculture/thekeepersfaqs.htm)) (context: NPS Cape Hatteras keepers page (a US station record).) — but Stannard Rock keepers rotated off after about three weeks, had no families, and their only named pastime was cribbage; a 1904 relief delay left them without food. ([Stannard Rock Light: The Loneliest Place in The World - Amusing Planet](https://www.amusingplanet.com/2020/01/stannard-rock-light-loneliest-place-in.html)) (context: Stannard Rock, Lake Superior, a remote station.)
  - Offshore keepers worked about two weeks at the light, then one week ashore. ([Keeper's Life (Chesapeake Chapter, US Lighthouse Society, Cheslights Kids)](https://www.cheslights.org/cheskids/html/keepers-life.htm)) (context: Cheslights general account of offshore keepers.) — but Bell Rock rotas ran six weeks on and two off, later two months on and one month off, and by the 1970s one on and one off. ([Lighthouse keeper duties (National Records of Scotland)](https://nrscotland.gov.uk/learning-and-events/for-the-safety-of-all-scotlands-lighthouses/lighthouse-keeper-duties/)) (context: NRS Scotland account of the Bell Rock and later Scottish stations, by era.)
  - Winding was every 90 minutes, and the weight 'no longer exists' once automated. ([The Automation of Lighthouses (Ways of Life, Substack)](https://waysoflife.substack.com/p/the-automation-of-lighthouses)) (context: Substack essay on Scottish automation.) — but The NRS page says the bells were rung 'roughly every 30 minutes'; it gives no winding interval. The 30-minute figure in the helper notes was attached to winding, but the page ties it to the bells. ([Lighthouse keeper duties (National Records of Scotland)](https://nrscotland.gov.uk/learning-and-events/for-the-safety-of-all-scotlands-lighthouses/lighthouse-keeper-duties/)) (context: NRS Scotland duties page. Flagged because two helper bricks and one experience goal use 30 minutes as a winding interval.)
  - Keepers' wives held a sewing circle, parties and birthday cakes, and the family shared the work and kept gardens and animals. ([Apostle Islands Scrapbook (McLean)](https://www.bobmackreth.com/Scrapbook/mcclean.htm), [Keeper's Life (Chesapeake Chapter, US Lighthouse Society, Cheslights Kids)](https://www.cheslights.org/cheskids/html/keepers-life.htm)) (context: Apostle Islands scrapbook (Lake Superior family stations) and Cheslights (land-light families).) — but Stannard Rock had no wives or families allowed, and some US 'stag lights' were run by men alone; a remote station wife said she gave up almost everything else. ([Stannard Rock Light: The Loneliest Place in The World - Amusing Planet](https://www.amusingplanet.com/2020/01/stannard-rock-light-loneliest-place-in.html), [Lighthouse keeper - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lighthouse_keeper), ["When a woman marries a lighthouse keeper..." (NPS)](https://www.nps.gov/apis/learn/historyculture/ihatelighthouses.htm)) (context: Stannard Rock and stag-light stations; a remote station wife's account.)
  Surprises:
  - Tower upkeep was paid by 'light dues' on shipping tonnage, so the ships that used the light paid for it. Nobody asked who paid for the light. ([The Automation of Lighthouses (Ways of Life, Substack)](https://waysoflife.substack.com/p/the-automation-of-lighthouses))
  - Boston Light was automated in 1998 but kept a staffed keeper, Sally Snowman, until she retired in 2023, so the US lost its last one then. ([Boston Light has stood since 1716 and was automated in 1998, but Congress kept a keeper on it (inkl)](https://www.inkl.com/news/boston-light-has-stood-since-1716-and-was-automated-in-1998-but-congress-kept-a-keeper-on-it-when-sally-snowman-retired-in-2023-the-us-lost-its-last-one))

  Surprises:

  - The real keeper's job already has a clock ritual: the weight is wound and released at the moment the lamp is lit, and each keeper stood a 4-hour night watch rotated daily.
